title: Elon Musk hints at future of software engineers, says there will be no lines of code
key_facts: An X user wrote 'Soon the entire world will be running on code that nobody has read'; Musk replied '100 percent'
Musk added there won't be lines of software as we know them, just machine code
Indeed Hiring Lab (via CNBC): US software job postings up nearly 15% since Feb 2025
Senior roles were 71% of the increase from May 2025 to May 2026; AI-titled roles 37%
Stanford 2026 AI Index: employment of 22-25 year-olds in AI-exposed fields down 16%, early-career developers down 20%
BLS projects developer jobs up 10% from 2025 to 2035
quote_evidence: Musk agreed with the prediction, replying, "100 percent." He then added, "There won't be lines of software as we know them, just machine code."
This does not establish that AI alone caused the decline, but it adds to concerns about entry-level opportunities.
why_it_matters_hint: The forecast touches the future of programming work.
notes: Full text read (India Today's AMP page; repeated text ignored). The jobs figures come from Indeed and Stanford as cited by India Today; the Stanford note says AI alone is not shown to have caused the decline. 'SpaceX and Tesla' title is general knowledge, not in the article.
